patterns.comment: A header field holds a string, and TiddlyWiki renders three of them as wikitext: text carries the tiddler body, and the core transcludes caption and description bare, which parses what they hold. A rule inside a capture opens mid-line, so the block rules anchored on ^ stand aside and the inline ones — a macro call, a transclusion, a link — reach the value as a reader meets it.
patterns.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5

patterns.comment: A control character alone breaks a field name; TW5 v5.2.x admits every other character in one.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.field.name.tiddlywiki5

3.comment: A header field value carries a plain string
3.name: string.unquoted.field.value.tiddlywiki5

dictionary-entry.comment:
One entry of a tiddler dictionary: a key, a colon, and a value TiddlyWiki renders as wikitext.

A dictionary key names no tiddler field, so the allow-list above — text, caption, description — reads nothing here: a dictionary carrying an entry called `caption` carries a key of that name and not a caption. Every value takes the wikitext reading instead, which the ground supports: of 2863 entries across TiddlyWiki’s own 28 dictionaries, 958 carry a wikitext construct, most of them a `<<colour ...>>` call in a palette.

The scopes come from the field reading above rather than from names of their own. An entry carries a key and a value, the reading matches, and a scope of its own would ask the corpus for ground that says nothing new.
dictionary-entry.name: meta.tiddler.field.tiddlywiki5
